transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because something happened at work. I pushed ahead with an onboarding launch before the approvals were actually in place, and I committed company money and vendor time. At the time it felt bold, like it had to happen and I was doing the necessary thing, but now I’m on leave and people keep asking what I was thinking.
Did you feel like you thought through the potential consequences before you decided to move ahead with the onboarding launch?

No, not really. At the time it didn’t feel like I needed to slow down and think through all of that. I pushed the onboarding launch forward and committed the company money and vendor time before the approvals were actually in place. It felt bold and necessary in the moment, like I was just making it happen. Now that I’m on leave, it looks very different, and everyone’s asking me what I was thinking.
Have you often acted on impulse like this before, without thinking through the consequences?

I don’t know if I’d say “often,” but this one was definitely like that. I pushed the onboarding launch ahead before the approvals were in place, and I committed company money and vendor time. In the moment it felt bold, like it needed to happen. Now I’m on leave, and people are asking me what I was thinking.
Have you acted on impulse like this in your personal life, outside of work?
I’m not really sure. Nothing comes to mind right away outside of work that feels like the same kind of thing. I’d have to think about it more.
Do you often find yourself acting impulsively in other areas of your life, such as in relationships or finances?

I can’t really point to relationships or finances the same way. The main thing I keep coming back to is the work situation — I pushed the onboarding launch forward and committed company money and vendor time before approvals were in place. At the time it felt bold and necessary, like I was doing what had to be done. Now I’m on leave, and everyone’s asking what I was thinking.
Have you acted impulsively like this since you were a teenager?
I’m not sure. I don’t really have a clear memory of acting like this back when I was a teenager. Nothing specific comes to mind.
Do you think you've generally acted impulsively throughout your adult life?

I don’t think so, not in a way I can clearly point to. I mean, I’ve made quick decisions like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve generally been impulsive throughout my adult life. This work situation is the main thing that stands out to me.
Have you ever gotten into trouble for violating rules or social norms in other contexts?

Not that I can really think of. I haven’t had a pattern of getting in trouble for breaking rules or doing socially inappropriate things in other areas. Nothing specific comes to mind beyond the work issue we talked about.
Would you say that acting on impulse without thinking through the consequences is generally how you approach decisions and actions?

No, I wouldn’t say that’s generally how I make decisions. I usually try to think things through, at least enough to understand what might happen. I’m not saying I never make a quick choice, but I don’t see myself as someone who normally acts without considering consequences.
Have you ever engaged in behavior that was intentionally deceitful or manipulative towards others?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve told white lies like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve intentionally tried to deceive or manipulate people as a pattern. Nothing like that really comes to mind.
Have you often done things that you knew would upset or harm others?
No, not often. I mean, I’ve had arguments or said things poorly like anyone, but I don’t go out of my way to upset people or hurt them. I can’t think of a pattern of doing that.
Have you generally considered the feelings of others before acting on your impulses?

I think so, generally. I try to consider how what I do might affect other people. I can be imperfect about it, especially if I’m frustrated, but I wouldn’t say I usually ignore other people’s feelings before acting.
Has this kind of impulsive behavior been a part of your personality for as long as you can remember?

No, I wouldn’t say it’s been part of my personality forever. This feels more recent. It’s been building for about a month, really since the new executive started pushing back on my onboarding redesign.
Have you ever had a period of time where you repeatedly engaged in behavior that could be considered irresponsible or reckless?

Yes. That’s basically why I’m here. I pushed ahead with the onboarding launch and committed company money and vendor time before the approvals were actually in place. At the time it felt bold and necessary, like I was just getting it done, but now I’m on leave and everyone’s asking what I was thinking.
Have you ever been in trouble with the law?
No, I haven’t been in trouble with the law. Nothing like arrests or charges.
Do you think this impulsive behavior at work is part of a larger pattern in your life or more of an isolated incident?

I think it’s more tied to what happened at work than some lifelong pattern. I mean, I’m here because I pushed the onboarding launch forward and committed company money and vendor time before the approvals were actually in place. At the time, it felt bold and necessary, like I was cutting through delays. But now I’m on leave, and people are asking what I was thinking, so… it clearly had real consequences.

I don’t think it’s my overall personality, at least not how I usually see myself. It feels more like I got caught up in that specific situation at work. I pushed the onboarding launch ahead and committed money and vendor time before the approvals were actually there. At the time it felt bold, like I was just doing what needed to be done, but now I’m on leave and everyone’s asking what I was thinking.

I don’t want to keep acting that way. Honestly, being on leave now has made it pretty clear there were real consequences. I pushed the onboarding launch ahead and committed company money and vendor time before approvals were in place, and at the time it felt bold and necessary. Now people are asking what I was thinking, so… I hope that makes me slow down next time.

I don’t think it has to always be that way. I mean, I’m here because I pushed ahead with the onboarding launch and committed company money and vendor time before the approvals were in place.
